title: Scattershot latency medianization sync — 2027-04-01
content:
Meeting: Scattershot latency medianization sync
Date: 2027-04-01
Attendees: Marisol (notes), Daniel, Connor, Priya, Aisha, two SRE rotation engineers
Location: weekly perf sync (video + huddle room C)
Purpose: capture weird non-monotonic latency spikes we've been seeing in mixed-sequence soak runs and align reproduction / next steps. Trying an experiment-focused run plan rather than broad benchmarks.

TL;DR:
- Observed repeated short (200ms-2s) P99 spikes during otherwise steady throughput in mixed-seq soak across two clusters (eu-west-1a and us-central-2b). Spikes correlate with small bursts of KV cache misses and transient GPU SM frequency drops on a subset of instances.
- P50 stable; P95 shows small bumps; P99 is unstable (10x variation vs baseline).
- Repro plan: targeted microsoak (4h) with pinned model variant + kernel set, NVML telemetry capture, and increased tracing sampling for sequence prefix churn.
- Immediate actions: run focused soak tonight with new tracing flags, collect NVML/GPU telemetry, add sidecar probe for kernel scheduling jitter, and open bisect job to compare q4f16 vs q8_0 quantized kernels.

Observations / Data:
- Run: mixed_seq_soak_2027-03-30 (12h), model: rw-infer-open-7b-16k-q4f16, seq dist: {mean 420, 90p 1800, 99p 5400} (mixed user queries + long context appends). Average QPS: 420 -> sustained across nodes.
- Baseline (quiet) P99: ~2800ms. During spike windows P99 jumped to 6–8s for short intervals (3–7 mins).
- Correlates found:
  * KV cache miss rate increased ~43% in spike windows (from 2.9% -> 4.1%).
  * NVML showed transient GPU SM frequency drops of ~10–12% on 2/24 nodes in us-central run. Drops last ~20–60s and align with latency spikes after 10–15s lag.
  * No corresponding CPU throttling or host OOMs observed.
  * Traces show a subset of requests experiencing additional kernel dispatch latency (~40–120ms extra per dispatch) — potentially kernel queueing due to device-side scheduling churn.
- Anecdotal: spikes concentrate on nodes running older driver 510.x vs 515.x. Need to confirm driver correlation (possible confounder).

Hypotheses:
1) Device frequency scaling + NV driver micro-pauses cause occasional kernel enqueue delays that amplify for long sequences (KV cache churn increases kernel count).
2) Mixed-seq workload increases prefix cache eviction churn -> more KV misses -> more GPU kernel launches -> bursts of small kernels increase scheduling pressure -> tail latency spikes.
3) Kernel variant selection (q4f16 path vs q8 path) interacts badly with scheduler under mixed kernel sizes leading to tail amplification.
4) Less likely: network fabric microbursts adding backend RPC delays (no link-level retransmits seen in capture but will re-run with tcpdump).

Repro / Experiment plan (priority ordered):
A) Focused microsoak (tonight 02:00 UTC, 4h window)
   - Target cluster: us-central-2b (replicate where SM drops seen)
   - Model: rw-infer-open-7b-16k-q4f16 pinned (no auto-fallback)
   - Config: kernel_set=v2.4, batching: continuous, batch_timeout_ms=6, max_batch_tokens=8192
   - Telemetry: NVML sampling 1s, dmesg+kern logs, per-kernel enqueue timestamps, KV cache hit/miss per request, perf counters (SM occupancy), and agent trace sample rate x2 baseline
   - Expected outcome: if driver/freq hypothesis true, NVML windows should align; if kernel-selection, we should see different kernel timings vs q8 path in bisect run.

B) Bisect kernel variant (parallel)
   - Split-run test harness comparing q4f16 vs q8_0 for identical traffic split (shadow traffic via shadow-run gating) for 3h each
   - Capture per-kernel latency histograms, kernel count per request, and prefix cache utilization

C) Driver experiment (non-prod repro): roll a small pool (4 nodes) to 515.x driver and re-run a short soak to validate driver correlation. If driver fixes the spikes, broaden rollout and schedule change window for production pools.

D) Tracing + probe adjustments
   - Increase sampling for requests hitting >1500 tokens; add sidecar probe to record kernel queue depth every 250ms (lightweight)
   - Add temporary log marker for kernel_set selection so we can attribute spikes to kernel path decisions.

Engineer's notes / shorthand (raw):
- Connor: "SM freq drops look like power management throttles — check BIOS p-state governors and node-level thermal variance logs"
- Daniel: "Observed kernel dispatch backlog in device-queue; attaching slew of extra small kernels when KV miss rate climbs"
- Priya: "Confirming host driver diff; 510.x nodes show >2x dispatch jitter variance vs 515.x sample"
- Aisha: "Will run tcpdump at 2s rotate, but not seeing fabric retransmits so deprioritize until kernel driver test done"

Open action items (owner — due):
- Night soak + telemetry capture (Marisol & SRE oncall) — 2027-04-01 02:00 UTC
- Kernel variant bisect harness (Connor) — 2027-04-01 18:00 UTC
- Driver mini-roll and short soak (Daniel) — 2027-04-02 03:00 UTC (non-prod pool)
- Add kernel_set marker logs and sidecar probe (Priya) — 2027-04-01 12:00 UTC
- Aggregate NVML + trace correlation script (Marisol) — 2027-04-02 09:00 UTC
- Post-mortem note skeleton (Aisha) — 2027-04-02 12:00 UTC

Follow-ups for next sync:
- Bring side-by-side histograms (q4 vs q8), NVML SM frequency timeline overlay, and KV miss timeline. If driver roll fixes, prepare rollback plan and release notes. If not fixed, pivot to kernel scheduling mitigations: coalescing small kernels on host or prefetch KV segments for long sequences.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider micro-batching within a request for long sequences so we reduce number of kernel launches at the cost of tiny added compute per token but potentially big tail improvement. Prototype in wasm-runner shim locally.
- Add a short Jenkins job that runs the bisect harness nightly for 1h to surface regressions early.

References / links (inlined):
- JIRA: JIRA-RI-7321 (scattershot tail investigation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/6123 (trace-sampling and nvml capture hooks)
- Slack: #serving-runtime thread (pinned: thread-83f2)

End notes: heavy experimental day. Keep the run reproducible and keep all telemetry archives until we sign off on root cause. If anyone sees similar spikes in Dedicated clusters, tag them in the JIRA.

-- Marisol
